notes.key_messages: Teachers should reinforce with all their candidates the need for full presentation of working, especially in questions where candidates are asked to prove a particular result. If necessary steps of working are omitted then full marks cannot be awarded. This applied particularly to Question 5 where often very good candidates failed to show sufficient working. Whilst Examiners will generally accept steps that can be done mentally or on a calculator, this does not apply to questions that require a rigorous proof. notes.general_comments: General comments While presentation of work for many candidates was satisfactory there were significant numbers of candidates whose work was untidy and difficult to follow. The rubric on the front of the Question Paper says ‘You are reminded of the need for clear presentation in your answers’. It is generally true that marks cannot be awarded if methods used are not clear. It is worth noting here a very common error: forgetting the ± sign. For example, in Question 8(ii), p² = 4  p = ±2. Mistakes of this kind were also seen in Questions 2(ii), 7, 9(i). Comments on specific questions
